checks.quote: The far detector (the improved ICARUS-T600) will be located in a new building 600 m from the BNB target.

geometry.locator: OSM way/1423112774, extract timestamp 2026-09-18; src:sbn-proposal-2015 'The far detector (the improved ICARUS-T600) will be located in a new building 600 m from the BNB target.'
geometry.note: No OpenStreetMap tag names the building; the positional match (603.1 m from the derived BNB target against the sourced 600 m, 0.7 degrees off the beam axis) is strong, and it is the only plausible candidate found in this area.

method: OSM way 1423112774 (unnamed building=yes footprint, 62.4 m from the MiniBooNE building at bearing 355.0 degrees -- i.e. on the far side of MiniBooNE from the BNB target) identified as the ICARUS-T600 (SBN far detector) hall by POSITION, not by an OSM name tag: it is 603.1 m from geometry:fermilab-bnb-target at an axis deviation of only 0.7 degrees, matching the sourced 600 m SBN far-detector baseline (src:sbn-proposal-2015) within 0.5%, and it is the only building anywhere near that expected distance/bearing in a wide-area search. Representation is 'derived' rather than 'georeferenced' because the identity attribution, not just the shape, rests on this positional match.
name: ICARUS-T600 hall (identity derived from position)
notes: The detector ran at Gran Sasso from 2010 to 2013 and was overhauled at CERN from 2014, so no Fermilab building stood for it in those years; the 2015 short-baseline proposal describes it as "a new building". The building is drawn from July 2017, when Fermilab News describes the detector arriving to be placed outside "the Short-Baseline Neutrino Far Detector building" until it is installed "inside the new ICARUS building"; the detector moved in on 14 August 2018 ("a recently completed building"). The building's own completion date is not given in the pages consulted.

summary.plain: The building that houses the ICARUS-T600 neutrino detector at Fermilab, identified by its position 600 m from the Booster Neutrino Beam target because no OpenStreetMap tag names it; drawn from July 2017.

valid.locator: Fermilab News, 2017-07-25, 'ICARUS detector scheduled to arrive at Fermilab today'; Fermilab News, 2018-08-16, 'ICARUS neutrino detector installed in new Fermilab home' ('a recently completed building')
valid.note: Start is the first date a source describes the building as standing; its completion date is not given in the pages consulted.
valid.quote: The 120-ton ICARUS detector will be located outside of the Short-Baseline Neutrino Far Detector building for the next couple of months until it is installed inside the new ICARUS building.
